text.title: Membership / Entailment / Neither Decision Tree
text.summary: Routing from the observable shape of an output field to a groundedness strategy. Run it once per field, not once per response — mixed outputs land in two different branches.

decision-tree.root-question: For this field, can every legal value be enumerated at request time from an artefact you supplied or control?

conclusion.verdict: Membership. Compute grounding_rate = |E n C| / |E| in code, drop or reject non-members, count them. No scorer, no judge, no threshold. Write the contract and stop.

Fix the request before the metric. Put the candidate set (or a deterministically narrowed slice of it) into the prompt so the model selects rather than recalls. Validating an authored identifier against a set the model never saw measures luck.
NOT closed. A set the model produced is asserted, not supplied; checking against it proves self-consistency only. Find the authoritative artefact or treat the field as open.
Neither. Do not claim-decompose a capped one-liner. Review it by sampling, or remove the cap and treat it as prose the product stands behind.

branch.when: enumerable == false AND field_is_prose == true AND stakes == 'high'

conclusion.verdict: Entailment, as triage only. HHEM-2.1-Open (Apache 2.0, CPU, ~1.5 s per 2k tokens) to rank output for human attention. Never a gate; never Bespoke-MiniCheck in a commercial product.

branch.when: enumerable == false AND field_is_prose == true AND stakes == 'low'

conclusion.verdict: Neither. Declare the field open in the contract, state that the grounding rate excludes it, and spend the budget on the closed fields where the answer is exact.
Overlay. The check is already right and unobservable. Promote the log line to a counter on the result object and assert on it in the eval harness before adding anything else.
